title: Priority credit reflow: stabilize continuous batcher under KV-heavy workloads
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Stabilizes continuous batching under KV-heavy loads by introducing a priority-credit reflow mechanism and adaptive soft timeouts. Reduces starvation of KV-pinned requests and smooths tail latency. No public API changes.
changes_summary:
Key changes across batcher and KV subsystems:
- src/runtime/batcher/scheduler.go: add priority-credit accounting, reflow loop and heuristics to drain credits from low-priority slots.
- src/runtime/batcher/credit_reflow.go: new component implementing credit decay, reflow windows and adaptive refill on soft timeouts.
- src/runtime/kv/cache_manager.go: expose pin-aware stats and per-slot weight hints used by the scheduler.
- src/runtime/batcher/timeouts.go: adjustable jittered soft-timeout logic tied to occupancy signals.
- integration-tests/batcher/kv_replay_test.go: new deterministic replay harness for KV-pin heavy traces.
- perf/benchmarks/continuous_batcher_real_trace.yaml: benchmark config and helper script.
- docs/ops/continuous-batcher-tuning.md: operator-facing knobs and recommended presets.
- examples/quickstart/batcher-tuning.ipynb: notebook walkthrough for reproducing perf numbers.

description:
Motivation: In long-running continuous-batcher workloads with a mix of small KV-pinned requests and large model-generating requests, we observed starvation of pinned requests and amplified tail latencies when the batcher filled with long-running tokens. Existing preemption heuristics are brittle under bursty KV traffic.

This PR introduces a priority-credit reflow mechanism that: (1) maintains a lightweight per-priority credit budget, (2) triggers a reflow window when soft-timeouts/jitter indicate a slot is held too long, (3) gracefully reclaims or reassigns credits from low-impact/low-priority slots to satisfy pinned short requests, and (4) adapts refill rates based on occupancy and KV pin statistics.

Design notes: The reflow controller is intentionally decoupled from kernel execution paths; it emits hints to the scheduler so kernel hot paths remain minimal. A new credit_reflow component keeps short histograms for slot hold times and uses EWMA to avoid reacting to single outliers. Soft timeouts are jittered to avoid synchronized drains across replicas.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation: credit accounting, reflow controller, scheduler hook
- [x] Tests: unit coverage for credit logic, deterministic integration replay for KV scenarios
- [x] Benchmarks: real-trace perf harness added and baseline recorded
- [x] Docs: operator tuning guide and recommended presets
- [x] Safety: feature gated behind runtime flag 'batcher.priority_credit_reflow' (off by default in release channel)

Testing and roll-out: Feature gated and shipped behind a config flag. Rolling canary to Dedicated then Hosted; default remains off for customers until we validate in production canaries. If regressions observed, we auto-disable via runtime gate and fallback to previous scheduler behavior.

test_plan:
- Unit tests for credit accounting and scheduler hook.
- Integration replay: 10-minute KV-heavy trace run comparing main vs this branch using deterministic seed.
- Perf benchmark: real-client trace over 100k requests measuring p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput.
- Canary rollout: enable flag on 2 dedicated pools (staging), monitor P99 and error rates for 24h before enabling broader fleet.
benchmark_results:
Staging perf runs (real-trace):
- Baseline (main): p50=22ms p95=110ms p99=340ms throughput=13.5k rps
- This PR (flag=true): p50=24ms p95=95ms p99=210ms throughput=13.1k rps
Notes: small p50 regression (due to occasional preemptive credit moves) but substantial p95/p99 improvement for KV-heavy tails; end-to-end token cost delta ~+0.8% under this trace. Under mixed workloads (50/50 KV/generation) throughput within 3% of baseline.
risk_and_mitigation:
Risks: aggressive reflow could harm throughput if credits are reclaimed too eagerly; per-tenant fairness complications; potential interaction with existing hedging logic.
Mitigations: runtime gate and operator knob to cap controller CPU, EWMA smoothing to prevent oscillation, integration tests that run under synthetic heavy load, canary rollout with automatic rollback on P99 regressions, interaction tests with hedging and kv-pin logic added.
notes_for_ops:
Operator knobs (docs/ops/continuous-batcher-tuning.md):
- batcher.priority_credit_reflow (bool)
- batcher.reflow_window_ms (int, default 60)
- batcher.reflow_jitter_pct (int, default 15)
- batcher.controller_cpu_budget_pct (int, default 2)
- batcher.per_tenant_credit_override (map in tuning config)
Recommended initial preset: "balanced-kv" (enabled on dedicated staging only).
